title: Seed, Clone and Genetics Inventory Control

content.overview: A crop plan is only as traceable as its genetics inventory. Commercial names can change or be reused, so internal accessions, seed lots, clone sources and breeding generations need stable identifiers.

vocabulary.definition: A defined quantity of seed with common production and traceability history.
A stable internal identifier for a genetic source or retained line.
An alternate name retained as metadata without replacing the stable internal identity.

sections.title: Names are not enough
sections.body: Cultivar names alone do not prove genetic identity. Preserve source, accession, aliases, pedigree and retained-reference information where available.

sections.title: Generation and family matter for seed
sections.body: F1, F2, selfed or backcross labels describe population history only when parentage and lot identity are traceable.

sections.title: Inventory should preserve condition and location
sections.body: Record quantity, storage location, receipt/production date and any germination or identity verification so planning does not depend on assumed availability.

workedExamples: Two bags carrying the same cultivar name remain separate seed lots if produced from different parents or dates.
A renamed breeding line keeps the original accession and alias history instead of becoming a new identity.
commonMistakes: Using package names as primary keys.
Mixing seed generations into one inventory balance.
content.practicalApplication: Create a genetics ledger with accession, type, cultivar/alias, source, parentage/generation, lot, quantity, location and verification notes.
content.summary: Stable genetics inventory prevents naming errors from propagating into crop records, assessments and breeding history.
